subject: Clarify retroactive capacity charge — Q2 billing amendment
messages:
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@finserve.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@finserve.com>, Finance Billing <billing@finserve.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected retro charge on Aug invoice — need clarification

Hi Olga,

We just received our August invoice and noticed a one-time line item labeled "Retroactive capacity adjustment (Q2 usage)" for $24,350. This is a pretty material surprise for our finance team — we didn't anticipate any retro charges after the renewal. Can you help explain: which usage window this covers, why it was charged retroactively, and whether there's any supporting breakdown we can share with our auditors?

I've attached the invoice excerpt and our internal cost allocation doc. Happy to hop on a call this week if that's easier.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Barnes
Head of Procurement
FinServe Ltd

Attachments: finserve-invoice-aug2026.pdf (pdf), internal-cost-alloc.xlsx (xlsx)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected retro charge on Aug invoice — need clarification

Forwarding FinServe's note — their FP&A flagged a retroactive charge on Aug invoice they didn't expect. Alicia copied billing and Tom.

Quick summary: during a post-renewal audit we applied a Q2+ burst true-up to align committed capacity vs observed consumption for the period Apr–Jun; this resulted in the one-time adjustment. I have the usage CSV and the math.

Can you two confirm:
- whether this matches the batch-run reconciliation we did on 2026-08-30 (Rishi)
- whether there's an approved communications cadence for these kinds of post-renewal adjustments (Vivek)

I expect FinServe will want a plain-language explanation + a cleaned CSV they can hand to auditors.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: finserve-q2-usage-breakdown.csv

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected retro charge on Aug invoice — need clarification

Olga — confirmed. We ran the reconciliation job on 2026-08-30 against the committed capacity in the renewal (FS-2025-EXP-88). Findings:

- Observed consumption Apr 1–Jun 30: 3.8M token-seconds (total inference time equivalent in our billing model).
- Committed capacity for that quarter per renewal: 2.5M token-seconds.
- Delta billed as one-time adjustment: 1.3M token-seconds x $0.018/token-second = $23,400. After rounding and VAT adjustments it became $24,350 on their invoice.

Notes: the renewal contract has language that allows retrospective balancing of committed capacity vs observed usage for the quarter following renewal; legal signed off in 2026-06. We did not proactively send an interim notice before invoicing — that was my oversight.

Action items I propose:
1) Send FinServe a clear reconciliation CSV with line-by-line usage by date (we have that in the attached file).
2) Offer a one-time courtesy credit of $2,000 to acknowledge the communication gap (subject to approval).
3) Provide a short explanation of the clause in the contract pointing to section 3.4 (capacity and balancing).

I can draft the customer note; would like confirmation from Vivek on the credit.

- Rishi
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected retro charge on Aug invoice — need clarification

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear breakdown. I'm okay with a limited courtesy credit given the communication miss. Proposed adjustment:

- One-time credit: $2,000 (applied to next invoice)
- Keep the invoice as-is for accounting/audit trace, but issue a formal customer letter + reconciliation CSV and a small explanatory note referencing section 3.4 of the renewal.
- No changes to the contracted committed capacity; suggest we add a short process note to avoid surprises in future renewals.

Olga — you can send the explanation and the reconciliation CSV to Alicia. I'll approve the $2k credit and notify Billing to flag the account for the credit on the Oct invoice. Rishi, can you prepare the reconciled CSV and the digestible paragraph for customers?

Vivek
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks for flagging this and apologies for the surprise — I should have looped you ahead of the invoice. Below is a plain-language summary and attached is the line-level CSV that maps daily calls to the billed adjustment.

Summary (plain language):
- What happened: During the post-renewal consumption audit we found that actual usage in Q2 (Apr–Jun) exceeded the committed capacity in your renewal by ~1.3M token-seconds. Our billing policy triggers a one-time balancing adjustment to align charges for the quarter after renewals.
- Why it was billed now: The reconciliation job completed on Aug 30 and the adjustment was included on the Aug invoice to keep accounting records intact.
- What we're doing to make this right: We've approved a one-time courtesy credit of $2,000 to acknowledge the lack of prior communication; this will be reflected on your October invoice. We are not changing the historical invoice (so audit trails remain clear) but are providing the CSV + this explanatory note so your auditors have documentation.

Attached: finserve-q2-usage-breakdown.csv (line-level usage and calculations), proposed-adjustment-invoice-20260914.pdf (PDF copy of the invoice with explanatory line items).

If you prefer a short call to walk through the CSV, I'm available Wednesday morning (09:00–11:00 PT). Otherwise please confirm receipt and whether the $2,000 credit is acceptable.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0134

Hi Olga — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the CSV. We received everything and have passed it to our auditors; the breakdown is helpful. The $2,000 credit is acceptable.

One operational request for future renewals: can Redwood notify us within 7 business days when a post-renewal reconciliation triggers a material adjustment (> $5k)? That would help avoid surprises on our monthly close.

If you agree, can we add that commitment to the post-renewal checklist (email notification to procurement + billing)? Thanks again.

Best,
